{{Short description|Estonian biologist, environmentalist, and politician}}

[[File:Aleksei Lotman, 2011.jpg|thumb|Aleksei Lotman in 2011]]
'''Aleksei Lotman''' (also known as '''Alex Lotman''' and '''Aleks Lotman'''; born 6 May 1960 in [[Leningrad]]) is an [[Estonia]]n biologist, [[environmentalist]] and politician.

From 2010 to 2011 Lotman served as the leader of political party [[Estonian Greens]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Aleksei Lotman was elected as the new chairman of Greens' Party in Estonia|url=http://www.baltic-course.com/eng/baltic_news/?doc=5311|work=The Baltic Course|accessdate=25 October 2013|date=9 June 2010}}</ref> From 2007 to 2011, Lotman was a member of Estonian parliament [[Riigikogu]], representing the Estonian Greens. He was also leader of the parliamentary group for [[Tibet]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Estonia Forms A New Parliament Support Group for Tibet|url=http://www.thetibetpost.com/en/news/international/1595-estonia-forms-a-new-parliament-support-group-for-tibet|work=Tibet Post International|accessdate=25 October 2013|date=8 April 2011}}</ref> In the 2011 election, the Greens lost all their parliamentary representation.<ref>{{cite web|title=Estonian Elections 2011: Live Blog in English!|url=http://elections2011.estonianfreepress.com/|work=Estonian Free Press|accessdate=25 October 2013|date=March 7, 2011|archive-date=6 March 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160306090827/http://elections2011.estonianfreepress.com/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Since then he has worked for the [[Estonian Fund for Nature]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Eesti mahetootja Saidafarm pälvis rahvusvahelise Läänemere-sõbraliku talu tiitli|url=http://www.e24.ee/1362440/eesti-mahetootja-saidafarm-palvis-rahvusvahelise-laanemere-sobraliku-talu-tiitli|accessdate=25 October 2013|newspaper=E24 (Estonia)}}</ref>

He was awarded the [[Order of the National Coat of Arms]], 5th Class, by the President of Estonia on 6 February 2006.<ref name="teenetemärk">{{cite web|title=Teenetemärkide kavalerid|url=http://www.president.ee/et/vabariik/teenetemargid/kavalerid.php?tm=riigivapi&y=2006&pg=5|publisher=Vabariigi Presidendi Kantselei|accessdate=22 October 2013}}</ref>

Aleksei Lotman graduated from the [[Miina Härma Gymnasium|Tartu Miina Härma Secondary School No 2]] in 1978, and the [[University of Tartu|Tartu State University]] as a biologist in 1985.<ref name=majanduslugu/>

1991–2000, Lotman served as the vice director of the [[Matsalu National Park]].<ref name=majanduslugu>{{cite web|title=Lotman, Aleksei (1960)|url=http://www.eestimajandus.ee/moodul.php?moodul=CMS&Komponent=Lehed&id=1011&sm_id=1149|publisher=Eesti Majanduslugu|accessdate=22 October 2013|language=Estonian}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Alex Lotman is the son of literary scholar, semiotician, and cultural historian [[Juri Lotman]] and literary scientist [[Zara Mints]]. His brothers are literature researcher and politician [[Mihhail Lotman]] and artist Grigori Lotman. Alex Lotman is married to environmentalist Kaja Lotman, they have two daughters and a son.<ref>G. Egorov 2011. {{Deprecated archive|url=https://archive.today/20131024010031/http://g-egorov.livejournal.com/82409.html|title=Внучка великого филолога Ю.М.Лотмана пошла по стопам отца, но не деда.}}</ref>
